title: Суши во французском ресторане  (Sushi in a French Restaurant)

segments.t: Focused on sushi in a french restaurant, The Chef argues with Kristina about serving sushi in a French restaurant. Kristina reveals that Vika no longer works there. Let's listen closely to Chef Viktor and Kristina's exchange in Russian first, and then walk through each line together.
Кстати, Вика у нас не работает.
Now let us examine the conversation line by line.
'We have a French restaurant.' Chef Barinov uses the classic Russian possession phrasing — literally 'at us' rather than a verb meaning 'to have', combining 'French' with 'restaurant'.
'And not Japanese.' Chef Barinov delivers a punchy one-word reaction built around the Russian word meaning 'Japanese'.
'I adore sushi.' Kristina chooses the imperfective verb meaning 'adore' for the ongoing action, followed by 'sushi'.
'I eat them every day.' Kristina chooses the imperfective verb meaning 'to eat' for the ongoing action, followed by 'every' and 'day'.
'And what if you want khachapuri?' Chef Barinov turns a statement into a question purely through rising intonation on the word meaning 'you want', followed by 'khachapuri'.
'I will call a khachapuri maker.' Kristina uses the perfective verb meaning 'will call' to focus on the single completed result, pairing it with 'khachapuri baker'.
'I know how to cook khachapuri.' Senya chooses the imperfective verb meaning 'to know how to' for the ongoing action, followed by 'to cook' and 'khachapuri'.
'Shut up and get out.' The verb for 'went' is in the masculine past tense, marked by the '-l' ending.
'It is impossible to talk to you.' Chef Barinov puts the word for 'impossible' together with 'to talk' in a crisp, natural spoken turn of phrase.
Кстати, Вика у нас не работает.
'By the way, Vika doesn't work for us.' Kristina uses the classic Russian possession phrasing — literally 'at us' rather than a verb meaning 'to have', combining 'by the way' with 'works'.
'Did you fire her?' Russian forms this yes-or-no question without a question word, relying on rising pitch on 'to fire'.
'She quit herself.' The reflexive ending on the verb for 'quit' turns the action back onto the subject. Now let's listen to the whole conversation again from start to finish.
Кстати, Вика у нас не работает.

The Chef argues with Kristina about serving sushi in a French restaurant. Kristina reveals that Vika no longer works there. Next time you watch the episode, listen for the Russian expressions for 'restaurant' and 'to adore' — you will catch every word right away. See you in the next scene.

lines.fragment: Ну, у нас ресторан французской кухни,
А если завтра ты захочешь хачапури?
Ну, значит, я вызову хачапурщика, Вить.
Да ты-то заткнись, пошел вон отсюда.
Кстати, Вика у нас больше не работает.
